facts.name: Blue Vervain
facts.moisture: Moist to wet; good in a rain garden
facts.notes: Branched candelabras of thin violet-blue spikes that open from the bottom up through late summer. A Michigan wet-meadow native for rain gardens and damp spots, loved by bees and butterflies. Short-lived, but it reseeds without taking over, and its bitter leaves keep most animals away.

sources.title: Michigan Wildflower Farm: Wetland species list

garden.title: Romence Gardens (Grand Rapids garden center): Verbena hastata
garden.note: Sold at a Grand Rapids garden center; 2 to 5 ft tall, full to part sun, zones 3 to 9, deer resistant.

sources.title: New Moon Nursery: Verbena hastata plant page
sources.note: 2 to 6 ft tall; blooms July and August for about six weeks; full or part sun in moist to wet soil; zones 3 to 9; bitter leaves most animals won't eat.

companions.why: Surround blue vervain with wet-meadow plants such as ironweed, monarda, purple coneflower, golden Alexanders and mountain mint for a colorful, pollinator-friendly planting.
